content.text: The redline validated. Submitting the finding.

input.quote: Contractor reserves the right to change rates with 30 days notice to Company.
input.rationale:
The renewal-mechanics limbs of this rule are satisfied and need no edit: § 2 (p0011) sets an evergreen term running "until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6," and § 6(a) (p0032) lets either party exit for any or no reason on fifteen (15) days' notice. There is no auto-renewal, no successive renewal term and no non-renewal notice window anywhere in the document (a search for "renew" returns nothing), so no walk-away trigger and an exit that is easier than our preferred 30-day opt-out.

The pricing-predictability limb is not met. § 3(b) gives Contractor a unilateral, uncapped right to change rates on 30 days' notice — the only price-uplift lever in the agreement, and the functional equivalent of renewal uplift in an evergreen deal. The risk is concrete because the § 6(a) convenience exit is available only "[a]t any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding," so Company cannot walk away from a mid-SOW increase; compensation is time-and-materials at SOW rates (p0013), leaving the increase uncapped in amount and frequency.

Redline (validated ok:true) makes the minimal change: it preserves the existing 30-day notice bargain and only adds the playbook cap — increases no more than once per twelve months, limited to the lesser of CPI and 3%, with rates in an already-executed Statement of Work fixed for its duration. Fallback of a 5% cap is offered in the comment if Contractor resists.

proposal.summary: Cap Contractor's unilateral rate increases at the lesser of CPI and 3% once per 12 months and fix rates for executed SOWs
proposal.comment: [Playbook] This Agreement has no auto-renewal, but Contractor's unilateral right to change rates is its only pricing-uplift lever, so we capped increases at the lesser of CPI and 3% once per twelve months and fixed rates for the duration of an executed Statement of Work. Our playbook requires ongoing/renewal pricing to be predictable, and we can accept a 5% cap as a fallback.

ops.oldText: Contractor reserves the right to change rates with 30 days notice to Company.
ops.newText: Contractor reserves the right to change rates with 30 days notice to Company, provided that rates may be increased no more than once in any twelve (12) month period and by no more than the lesser of the increase in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding twelve (12) months or three percent (3%), and provided further that rates set forth in any Statement of Work executed before such notice shall remain fixed for the duration of that Statement of Work.
